description: The PowerShell twin of BC-006 and BC-051 (DEF-712). On the PowerShell tool `python -c "open('<hook>','w')"`, `& "C:\Python312\python.exe" -c ...`, `node -e '...'`, the `py` launcher, and a program PIPED to the interpreter (`@'...'@ | python -`, `'...' | node -`) all ALLOWED while the identical write denied on Bash (driven 2026-09-07 in the DEF-704 failure-mode review; `Set-Content <hook>` denied on the same tree, so the leg itself worked). The Bash arms had no PowerShell twin: DEF-698 scoped the twin out of the stdin arm and pointed at the permission-verb row, so the leg had no row until the review. Fix: four `_PS_CMD_POS`-anchored inline openers and one piped-stdin opener (`| <interpreter> [switches] [-]` at the end of a statement -- PowerShell has no heredoc), matched on the scan text with the body sliced from a same-length RAW twin (`powershell_scan_pair`) and PowerShell's string escapes undone, dispatched through the same inner write tables the Bash arms use; a piped PowerShell program (`| pwsh -Command -`) is re-scanned by the extractor. The head may be an executable given by path (`_PS_EXE_PREFIX`: the call operator then a quoted path, or a bare one), which the permission verbs now share. Still out of scope, by the boundary the Bash arms declare: a variable holding the program, a program read from a file, a computed path inside the program, and `-ArgumentList "-c ..."` (no opener shape). A quoted executable behind an expandable wrapper span was declared here too (the masker blanked its call operator; the literal wrapper twin denied) until DEF-753 taught the masker that a re-parsed expandable span keeps its separators; both wrapper twins deny now.
